title: TORCHLIGHT DEPTHS
evidence_quotes: Create one complete, self-contained HTML file for TORCHLIGHT DEPTHS, a self-playing 3D isometric dungeon explorer game in three.js that needs no user input (the player can take over at any time): a lone adventurer carrying a burning torch in one hand and a sword in the other explores a gritty stone dungeon, room by room, by torchlight. | Use a dark, gritty, lovingly lit aesthetic. The camera is a true isometric-style view (orthographic or a long-lens perspective at a classic three-quarter angle from above) that follows the player smoothly. | LIGHT IS THE STAR: the player's torch is a flickering warm point light that casts real moving shadows of pillars, crates, bars and monsters across the floor and walls; wall torches and braziers in sconces throw their own warm pools of light; a few cold accents (a blue glow from a magic rune, moonlight through a grate) contrast with the warm fire; embers and sparks drift up from every flame; dust hangs in the torch beams. | Build the dungeon in code: rough stone-block walls with cut-away fronts so the isometric camera can always see the player, flagstone floors with cracks, moss and puddles that reflect the firelight, wooden doors, iron-barred cells, pillars, stairs down, rubble, barrels, crates, bones, cobwebs, chests, banners and a few traps (spike plates, a swinging blade); rooms linked by corridors, with a sense of going deeper. | Monsters roam: skeletons, giant rats and a slime or two, each readable by torchlight with a small glow in their eyes. | The PLAYER is a small, clearly built adventurer (hooded cloak, armour, a torch held high casting the main light, a sword) with a proper walk cycle, a sword swing with a clear arc and impact, a hit flinch, and a torch that sways with each step. | SELF-PLAYING, WITH OPTIONAL CONTROLS: the hero plays itself from the moment the page loads and never needs a key, click or touch, but the player can take over at any time with WASD or the arrow keys to move and Space to attack (a gamepad works too); after a few seconds without input, the hero goes back to playing itself, and it never gets stuck on walls, doors or props. | ENEMIES MUST BE PRESENT AND ACTIVE: every room and most corridors hold monsters that are clearly visible on screen (skeletons, giant rats, slimes, and a bigger boss monster on every third level), they notice the hero, approach and attack, and the hero fights them in frequent, readable sword fights with swings, hits, knockback, hit flashes and monsters collapsing or bursting into bones and goo; a fight should be on screen most of the time, never long stretches of an empty dungeon. | A small HUD shows health hearts, gold, depth and monsters slain, in a crisp pixel font. | Add synthesized sound with Web Audio: footsteps on stone, the crackling torch, sword swings and hits, monster squeals, coins, a door unlocking and a low dungeon drone; because browsers gate audio behind a gesture, show only a small, unobtrusive "click for sound" hint in a corner that enables audio when clicked; the game itself starts and runs immediately without it and never waits for any input. | Make it fill the window, resize cleanly, run smoothly at 60 fps and start with zero console errors. | Deliver it as a single self-contained HTML file; any libraries are allowed.

title: Image-Blaster: Single Photo to Fully Playable 3D World
evidence_quotes: Feed it one image, get back a complete 3D world: 3D object meshes, a static environment, lighting, and ambient sound, all generated and assembled by Claude. | You drop a photo into a folder and Claude looks at the scene, then orchestrates a chain of models to rebuild it in 3D. | It generates a separate 3D mesh (.glb/.obj) for every object you want, builds the static room environment as a Gaussian splat, adds object-specific and ambient sound effects, and bakes in lighting. | Claude is the orchestrator. It picks objects out of your image, generates a clean reference image for each, sends those to a 3D generation model for meshes and materials, then sends the cleaned-up room to World Labs to build the explorable environment. | The output isn't locked in. It's just files on your computer, so you can drag the whole thing into Unity, Unreal, Godot, Blender, or a Three.js app and keep building.
